page: Amazon Web Services r4.8xlarge is a fourth-generation memory-optimized instance built on the Xen hypervisor. It is driven by an Intel Xeon E5-2686 v4 processor with an x86_64 architecture, delivering 32 dedicated vCPUs across 16 physical cores with multithreading enabled at a 2.3 GHz clock speed. The hardware configuration provides 244.0 GB of system memory, yielding approximately 7.62 GB per virtual core, alongside 45 MB of Level 3 cache. Network performance is anchored by a 12 Gbps baseline interface. The instance contains no bundled local NVMe storage and does not include GPU acceleration.

Benchmark evaluations reflect the characteristics of its Broadwell microarchitecture. Single-core performance occupies the lower tier across tests, with Geekbench and stress-ng single-threaded scores ranking in the bottom percentiles. Multi-core performance scales predictably across all 32 vCPUs, posting average scores of 16,338.44 in stress-ng and 20,329.52 in PassMark CPU tests. Memory read throughput reaches 61.25 GB/s in large uncached blocks, though uncached write throughput is comparatively weaker at 25.91 GB/s. High-concurrency operations remain robust, demonstrated by Redis SET performance measuring 19.71 million operations per second and stable database operation scores.

From an architectural standpoint, the r4.8xlarge offers significant memory density per core, but requires reliance on remote network volumes due to the absence of integrated local storage. Older microarchitecture tradeoffs mean lower single-thread instruction throughput compared to modern generations. Consequently, the instance is most appropriate for large in-memory caches, key-value stores such as Redis or Memcached, relational databases requiring expansive buffer pools, and ETL or batch processing tasks that are bottlenecked by memory capacity rather than peak single-core compute speed.
